## Kickoff Prompt for Antigravity (Single Agent Mode)

Copy and paste this into Antigravity to start the build:

---

You are building a production app for real users — not a demo, not a prototype. Every component, route, and test should be written as if this ships tomorrow.

Read every file in .gemini/antigravity/brain/ before doing anything else. These files are your source of truth:

- spec.md — what to build, feature priorities, acceptance criteria
- design-tokens.json — every color, font, spacing value (light mode only v1)
- copy.md — every piece of user-facing text, organized by page
- ui-rules.md — component patterns, animation rules, accessibility requirements
- api-contract.md — every API endpoint with request/response types and error formats

Also read .antigravity/rules.md for code quality and security rules you must follow.

Important context:
- Database is ALREADY deployed to Neon PostgreSQL via Prisma v7
- src/lib/db.ts is ALREADY configured with the driver adapter
- src/generated/prisma/ has the generated client — DO NOT re-run prisma generate
- No user auth in v1 — no accounts, no login
- Light mode only in v1
- 16 retailer sources (4 API + 12 scraped) — see api-contract.md
- Primary color: warm violet #7C3AED (use .600+ for text on white for WCAG AA)
- Two fonts: Inter (UI) and JetBrains Mono (prices/specs)

Build order:
1. Foundation — CSS variables, layout (header + footer + shell), shared components (laptop card, deal badge, price display, comparison tray, skeletons, empty states)
2. API layer — error handler, validators, all 7 public endpoints + 2 cron endpoints per api-contract.md
3. Retailer adapters — 16 sources implementing RetailerAdapter interface
4. Category browsing — Work, Gaming, Apple pages with filter sidebar + card grid
5. Spec & brand filtering — dynamic filters from /api/filters, URL param state
6. Sorting — 5 sort options wired to URL params
7. Search — typeahead from /api/search/suggestions, search results page
8. Laptop detail page — full specs, all retailer prices with buy links, review score
9. Top Deals page — sorted by discount %
10. Budget Picks page — best specs-to-price ratio
11. Best Rated page — highest review scores
12. Side-by-side comparison — compare checkboxes, sticky tray, comparison table (max 3)
13. Seed data — ~50 realistic laptops with prices from 3-5 retailers each
14. Homepage — CarGurus-style hero + deal sections

For each feature:
- Generate a plan artifact BEFORE writing code
- Build the API route first (with withErrorHandler + validateBody)
- Build the UI component (all 4 states: loading skeleton, error, empty, success)
- Write a unit test and an E2E test
- Run npm test before moving to the next feature

Use design tokens for ALL visual properties. Use copy.md for ALL text. No hardcoded colors. No placeholder text. No lorem ipsum.

Start with feature 1 now.
